n1e57df90199.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: only one date)
n1e57df90199.s: Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka granted Madras to Francis Day in 1639 during the reign of which Vijayanagara ruler?
n1e57df90199.x: The 1639 grant of Madras to Francis Day of the Machilipatnam council came in the reign of Venkatapati Raya III.

nf4aa43a0555.s: After the Battle of Talikota, Hampi was looted for about:
nf4aa43a0555.x: Hampi was looted for about six months; the damage was severe but not total.

nc00cfe025c2.s: Venkatapati Raya II permitted the Dutch to trade at:
nc00cfe025c2.x: Venkatapati Raya II permitted Dutch trade at Pulicat and also allowed Jesuit churches at Nellore and Chandragiri.

nddb62d251c4.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler was called the 'Second Andhra Bhoja'?
nddb62d251c4.x: Venkatapati Raya II was called the 'Second Andhra Bhoja' (and 'Second Krishnadevaraya').

n7cbb1e2f610.s: The Aravidu rulers of Vijayanagara originated from:
n7cbb1e2f610.x: The Aravidus came from Kurnool; after Talikota the empire's centre shifted to the Telugu country (Penukonda, Chandragiri).

na69552f26e0.s: The Nayaka kingdom of Tanjore was founded by:
na69552f26e0.x: Tanjore was founded by Sevappa Nayaka; Madurai by Vishwanatha Nayaka, Gingee by Krishnappa Nayaka and Mysore by Raja Wodeyar.

n88eca6c8f17.s: Who was the key organiser of the Deccan Sultanates' alliance that fought at Talikota (1565)?
n88eca6c8f17.x: Ibrahim Qutb Shah of Golconda was the key organiser of the coalition.

n1f06517c2e7.s: In 1546-47, by backing Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar, Rama Raya acquired the:
n1f06517c2e7.x: In 1546-47 Rama Raya supported Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar and took the Raichur doab.

n48e9796e37a.s: Among the marriage alliances before Talikota, Chand Bibi was married to:
n48e9796e37a.x: Chand Bibi married Ali Adil Shah, while Bibi Jamal married Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

n17da0502d30.s: The Tirumala Rayala Mahal at Madurai was built by:
n17da0502d30.x: Tirumala Nayaka, who ruled Madurai from 1623 to 1659, built the Tirumala Rayala Mahal.

na31efb1062f.s: At the time of Talikota, who was the Tuluva king of Vijayanagara with Aliya Rama Raya as regent?
na31efb1062f.x: Sadasiva Raya was the nominal Tuluva king and Rama Raya his regent.

n474cfc53984.s: Shaivarka Mani Dipika was written by:
n474cfc53984.x: Shaivarka Mani Dipika is the work of Appayya Dikshita; Vasucharitra is associated with Ramaraja Bhushanudu.

nc1d6fd7509b.s: The Aravidu dynasty was the ____ ruling dynasty of Vijayanagara.
nc1d6fd7509b.x: The Aravidu dynasty was the fourth dynasty of Vijayanagara and ruled from 1570 to 1680 with seven rulers.

n86965a2599f.s: After the defeat at Talikota, Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to:
n86965a2599f.x: They fled to Penukonda; Chandragiri became a capital later, under Venkata II.

n3ec8b5db5ec.s: Vishwanatha Nayaka was granted Madurai after capturing his rebel father, ____.
n3ec8b5db5ec.x: Vishwanatha Nayaka captured his rebel father Nagama and was granted Madurai; his son Krishnappa Nayaka made it independent c. 1565.

n7197e4334ad.s: Jagadeva Rao, whose sheltering by Rama Raya helped provoke the Deccan coalition, was a rebel from:
n7197e4334ad.x: Rama Raya sheltered Jagadeva Rao, a rebel from Golconda, one of the causes of the coalition.

n79bb8b4eae1.s: Berar, the Deccan Sultanate that stayed out of the alliance against Vijayanagara at Talikota, was ruled by the:
n79bb8b4eae1.x: Berar was ruled by the Imad Shahis and stayed out; Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar formed the alliance.

nd127499c25e.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Tulughma – Flanking units wheeling round to encircle the enemy
Ustad Ali and Mustafa – Ottoman gunners commanding Babur's artillery
Rumi method (araba) – War elephants chained together as a barrier
nd127499c25e.x: The Rumi method (araba) chained carts, not elephants, as a barrier for matchlockmen and guns.

n9b5ea07639f.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts carry no dates)
n9b5ea07639f.s: The first major field-artillery battle in North India was the:
n9b5ea07639f.x: Panipat I, in which Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, the last Delhi Sultan, was the first major field-artillery battle in North India.

n0f5be14110b.s: The Mansabdari system was introduced under:
n0f5be14110b.x: The Mansabdari system was introduced under Akbar, not during Babur's four-year rule.

n56e5ef054d4.s: Besides Daulat Khan Lodi and Alam Khan, Babur was invited to India by:
n56e5ef054d4.x: The three inviters were Daulat Khan Lodi (Governor of Punjab), Alam Khan (Ibrahim Lodi's uncle) and Rana Sanga of Mewar.

ne89f7d17396.s: After his victory at Khanwa, Babur took the title:
ne89f7d17396.x: After Khanwa Babur took the title 'Ghazi'; before the battle he had declared jihad, renounced wine and remitted tamgha for Muslims.

n40a751a9015.s: In his account of India, Babur praised which ruler as the most powerful?
n40a751a9015.x: Babur praised Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara as the most powerful ruler in India.

n4a62072d7bb.s: Babur's lavish distribution of the Lodi treasure after Panipat earned him the nickname:
n4a62072d7bb.x: Lavish sharing of the treasure earned him the nickname 'Qalandar'; 'Ghazi' was the title taken after Khanwa.

n1d0a9549821.s: The silver coins Babur issued in the Timurid style were called:
n1d0a9549821.x: Babur issued silver Shahrukhi coins in the Timurid style and introduced the charbagh garden.

n02eddbe6f25.s: At Babur's death, his dominions extended from Kabul and Badakhshan to the borders of:
n02eddbe6f25.x: Babur's dominions ran from Kabul and Badakhshan through Punjab, Delhi and Agra to the borders of Bihar.

nb1313edf903.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the revenue systems of Sher Shah and Akbar-Todar Mal?
o: Sher Shah classified land into three categories.
Sher Shah fixed the state's share at one-fourth of average produce.
Akbar-Todar Mal retained the one-third share but used ten-year averages.
Akbar-Todar Mal used four land classes: polaj, parauti, chachar and banjar.
nb1313edf903.x: Sher Shah's rate was one-third of average produce, not one-fourth; the other three statements are correct.

n5dfb2b32285.s: Besides lodging travellers, Sher Shah's sarais served as ____ for relaying news and mail.
n5dfb2b32285.x: The sarais served as dak-chowkis; market towns also grew around them.

n49d98e9c5fd.x: Sadak-e-Azam was the major road from Bengal to the Indus; the others were separate Sur routes.

nindian-history-62-12.x: The Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque was built inside the Purana Qila (Old Fort).

nb5321979334.s: Humayun died in January 1556 after falling from the stairs of the Sher Mandal library in:
nb5321979334.x: He fell from the stairs of the Sher Mandal library in the Purana Qila, Delhi.

n4a5a04dde0d.s: Under Sher Shah, the state's share of land revenue was fixed at:
n4a5a04dde0d.x: The state share was one-third of average produce; the system became the model for Todar Mal's Bandobast.

n6bfb7641104.s: Who succeeded Sher Shah on the Sur throne?
n6bfb7641104.x: Islam Shah (Jalal Khan) succeeded Sher Shah and ruled 1545-53.

n29265ea3835.s: Babur's last battle, fought in 1529 against the Afghans under Mahmud Lodi, was the Battle of:
n29265ea3835.x: Ghaghra (1529) was Babur's last battle; the order was Panipat I, Khanwa, Chanderi, Ghaghra.

nf019875bccd.s: Balban's Tomb, with the first true arch in India, is located at:
nf019875bccd.x: Balban's Tomb is at Mehrauli, Delhi; Sasaram has Sher Shah's octagonal tomb.

n8f0ec0acd9b.s: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah, contemporary of Babur, Humayun and Sher Shah, ruled Golconda from:
n8f0ec0acd9b.x: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah ruled Golconda from 1518 to 1543.

n83766e2928c.s: After the First Battle of Panipat, Babur occupied:
n83766e2928c.x: After Panipat Babur occupied Delhi and Agra.

na49916726f7.s: The Rumi method of warfare used by Babur was of ____ origin.
na49916726f7.x: The Rumi method (carts linked as a barrier for matchlockmen and artillery) was Ottoman; Tulughma was Uzbek.

n5c681d88161.s: Farid received the title 'Sher Khan' for slaying a tiger from:
n5c681d88161.x: The title 'Sher Khan' was given by Bahar Khan of Bihar, not Babur.

n71a074d1989.s: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought on:
n71a074d1989.x: Panipat II was fought on 5 November 1556; Hemu was struck in the eye by an arrow and captured.

n7cf185fcc35.s: In a Sur-era pargana, the Fotedar functioned as the:
n7cf185fcc35.x: The Fotedar was the pargana treasurer; Karkuns were the Hindi and Persian writers.

n420247b4fa2.s: To stop officers building local interests, Sher Shah's administration:
o: Gave officers their posts for life
Appointed officers in their home areas
n420247b4fa2.x: Officers were frequently transferred so that they did not build local interests.

n3ded4ce2b06.s: During his exile, Humayun retook Kandahar and Kabul with the help of:
n3ded4ce2b06.x: The Safavid Shah Tahmasp of Persia helped him retake Kandahar and Kabul.

n02dcb5e905d.s: At the Battle of Dourah (1532), Humayun defeated the Afghans and drove Mahmud Lodi from:
n02dcb5e905d.x: Dourah (Devara), 1532, on the Gomati, drove Mahmud Lodi from Jaunpur.

neef60953fc2.s: Jaita and Kumpa were generals of:
neef60953fc2.x: Jaita and Kumpa were Maldeo's generals at the hard-fought battle of Samel (1544).

n771e4386f7d.s: In Sur administration, the Chief Shiqdar (shiqdar-i-shiqdaran) of a sarkar looked after:
n771e4386f7d.x: The Chief Shiqdar handled law and order; the Chief Munsif was the sarkar revenue/civil officer.

n11e3e205031.x: Dagh was the branding of horses; chehra/huliya was the descriptive roll of soldiers.

n52c528f0210.s: The last Afghan dynasty to rule Delhi was the:
n52c528f0210.x: The Surs were the last Afghan dynasty to rule Delhi; Sher Shah's revenue, coinage and roads set the Mughal pattern.

nb302e156116.s: Sher Khan assumed the title 'Sher Shah' after the Battle of:
nb302e156116.x: He took the title Sher Shah after Chausa (1539); after Kannauj (1540) he took the throne.

n4e2b7c90542.s: In Sher Shah's currency, the dam was a coin of:
n4e2b7c90542.x: The rupiya was silver, the dam copper and the mohur gold.

nebef73d980f.s: Sher Shah's land survey measured land uniformly with the:
nebef73d980f.x: Land was measured with the sikandari gaz and the jarib, and classified into good, middling and bad.

nbc4297a041d.s: Sher Shah took the fort of Raisen from:
nbc4297a041d.x: Raisen was taken from Puran Mal.

nbec68be0777.x: The Baburnama was written in Chaghatai Turkish; Persian was the Mughal court language.

nindian-history-17-52.s: The Battle of Kannauj (1540), in which Sher Shah defeated Humayun, is also called the Battle of:
nindian-history-17-52.x: Kannauj is also called the Battle of Bilgram.

n8024bd338b7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Guru Tegh Bahadur?
o: He was the ninth Sikh Guru, born Tyag Mal in 1621.
He was executed by Jahangir in 1606.
n8024bd338b7.x: Execution by Jahangir in 1606 describes Guru Arjan Dev; Tegh Bahadur was executed on Aurangzeb's orders in Delhi in 1675.

n9c132a2a61b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Banda Singh Bahadur?
o: He was originally named Lachhman Dev.
His sovereign Sikh state had its capital at Anandpur Sahib.
He defeated Wazir Khan at Chappar Chiri and conquered Sirhind in 1710.
He was executed in Delhi in 1716 by Farrukhsiyar.
n9c132a2a61b.x: The capital of his Sikh state was Lohgarh; Anandpur Sahib was founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur.

n736670794da.x: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in 1679 and banned festivals such as Navroz.

n2438bf87753.s: Which Mughal emperor was known as 'Zinda Pir'?
n2438bf87753.x: Aurangzeb was known as Alamgir and Zinda Pir.

nec745d943c0.shape: NOT (no single confirmed fact suited a one-liner)
nec745d943c0.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of Akbar's Rajput policy?
o: Appointment of Rajputs to high posts
Immediate loss of autonomy for every Rajput state after submission
nec745d943c0.x: Submission could be followed by restoration of autonomy and honour, so blanket loss of autonomy was not part of the policy.

n5cb8a4598d0.s: Which Mughal emperor had the highest number of Hindu nobles and generals in absolute terms?
n5cb8a4598d0.x: Aurangzeb had the highest absolute number, many of them Marathas and Rajputs recruited during the Deccan wars.

n5b67f4b280c.s: Who translated the Baburnama into Persian?
n5b67f4b280c.x: Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, son of Bairam Khan, translated the Baburnama into Persian.

n43df49ce756.s: Dara Shikoh was a follower of which Sufi order?
n43df49ce756.x: Dara Shikoh followed the Qadiri order, associated with Abdul Qadir Jilani.

n486f49e08eb.x: Rani Durgavati opposed Akbar in Gondwana; Baz Bahadur in Malwa, Rana Udai Singh at Chittor, Surjan Rai at Ranthambore.

nindian-history-82-15.s: Mughal painting reached its zenith under:
nindian-history-82-15.x: Jahangir's reign was the peak of Mughal painting; Humayun laid its foundation.

n4d6160d5b44.s: Bhakta Ramadasu was related to Madanna and Akkanna as their:
n4d6160d5b44.x: Bhakta Ramadasu was the nephew of Madanna and Akkanna.

nf7bfd9aee3f.s: Mewar finally submitted to the Mughals under which emperor?
nf7bfd9aee3f.x: Mewar submitted under Jahangir through Amar Singh, whose son Karan Singh became a mansabdar.

n7387c0d207b.s: Akbar gave the title 'Jagat Guru' to the Jain scholar:
n7387c0d207b.x: Hiravijaya Suri was given 'Jagat Guru'; Jinachandra Suri received 'Yuga Pradhan'.

n6250c89ad19.s: Akbar built the Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri in:
n6250c89ad19.x: The Ibadat Khana was built in 1575; 1582 is the year of Din-i-Ilahi.

nb4cfb5f30e9.s: Which Mughal emperor, slightly more orthodox than Akbar, destroyed some newly built temples yet kept many Hindu nobles?
nb4cfb5f30e9.x: Shah Jahan was slightly more orthodox and destroyed some newly built temples but continued to employ many Hindu nobles.

n843f93b51e8.s: Bairam Khan, Akbar's regent (1556-60), was killed in 1561 while on his way to:
n843f93b51e8.x: Dismissed in 1560, Bairam Khan was killed on the way to Mecca in 1561.

n1063d462cb1.s: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi was known as:
n1063d462cb1.x: Sirhindi was Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani and propounded Wahdat-ul-Shuhud.

n536d55e5c30.s: The Mahzar of 1579, which made Akbar supreme arbiter in religious disputes, was drafted by:
n536d55e5c30.x: The Mahzar was drafted by Shaikh Mubarak.

need446c17e3.s: Din-i-Ilahi, joined by only a handful of people, lapsed with the death of:
need446c17e3.x: Din-i-Ilahi lapsed with Akbar and did not continue as a major institution.

nef284ffb126.s: Under Akbar, the Mahabharata was translated as the:
nef284ffb126.x: The Mahabharata was rendered as the Razmnama; the Atharvaveda was also translated.

o: A fixed cash rate per bigha
n2fbf360d1e9.x: Kankut estimated the standing crop; Batai was crop-sharing and Nasaq was based on past payments.

nindian-history-47-11.s: Tansen's early patron, Raja Ramchandra Singh, ruled:
nindian-history-47-11.x: Tansen was first patronised by Raja Ramchandra Singh of Rewa before joining Akbar's court as a Navaratna.

nindian-history-23-10.s: Under Aurangzeb's jizya, children below what age were exempted?
nindian-history-23-10.x: Children below 14 were exempt, along with women, slaves, beggars and the unemployed.

n23678d89ce2.s: Din-i-Ilahi did not become a mass religion mainly because it:
o: Was confined to the Rajput nobility
Was never forced on anyone and drew only a small circle
Was abolished by Akbar soon after its launch
Was banned by the ulema in 1579
n23678d89ce2.x: Its voluntary nature and small membership explain why Din-i-Ilahi never became a mass religion.

nindian-history-84-9.s: The Iranian court practice of Sijda (prostration) was abolished by:
nindian-history-84-9.x: Shah Jahan abolished Sijda; Akbar had acted against child marriage and Sati.

nindian-history-23-9.s: Along with the Banaras pandits, who petitioned Shah Jahan to abolish the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Allahabad?
nindian-history-23-9.x: Kavindracharya and the Banaras pandits sought the abolition of the pilgrim tax.

nindian-history-82-16.s: The Mughal Empire reached its maximum territorial extent under:
nindian-history-82-16.x: Aurangzeb's Deccan conquests of Bijapur and Golconda gave the empire its greatest extent.

nf7c40c49def.s: Akbar's empire stretched from Bengal to Afghanistan and from Kashmir to the:
nf7c40c49def.x: Akbar's empire extended from Bengal to Afghanistan and from Kashmir to the Godavari.

nindian-history-17-29.s: In the Battle of Haldighati (1576), the Mughal side was led by:
nindian-history-17-29.x: Man Singh led Akbar's forces against Rana Pratap at Haldighati in 1576.

n81a825e1e6f.s: Guru Gobind Singh, who fought 14 wars against Aurangzeb's forces, wrote the:
n81a825e1e6f.x: Guru Gobind Singh wrote the Zafarnama, which advocated the sword only when all other avenues failed.

na289a7fc6ca.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about land revenue in Qutb Shahi Golconda?
o: Land was classified as wet, dry, garden and waste.
The state generally took one-half of the produce.
Revenue was collected through amalguzars with hereditary deshmukhs and deshpandes.
The khalisa was expanded under Abdullah and Tana Shah.
na289a7fc6ca.x: Golconda generally took one-third of the produce, not one-half.

nc80fd84e019.s: Under the land revenue arrangement, the state share of one-third of average produce was paid in cash known as:
nc80fd84e019.x: The state share was paid in cash called dam, though payment in kind was allowed in some areas.

n8fd403ef53a.s: Under the Mughals, the Nasaq method of revenue assessment was mainly used in:
n8fd403ef53a.x: Nasaq was used mainly in Bengal; Batai in Thatta, Kabul and Kashmir, Zabti in the core provinces, plough-based assessment in parts of the Deccan.

n93bf8597687.s: Mughal crown land whose revenue went straight to the imperial treasury was called:
n93bf8597687.x: Crown land was khalisa; suyurghal and madad-i-maash were charitable revenue-free grants.

ne0663c69686.s: The head of a Mughal suba, served by a Diwan, Bakhshi, Sadr and Qazi, was the:
ne0663c69686.x: The Subedar headed the suba; the Diwan, Bakhshi, Sadr and Qazi were the other suba officials.

ndd9d5dee0b6.s: Under Akbar's Karori experiment (1574), each revenue circle was meant to yield:
ndd9d5dee0b6.x: Each circle was to yield one crore dams, hence the name 'karori'.

n0838e6c72bc.s: Akbar's Dahsala system was introduced in:
n0838e6c72bc.x: Dahsala, based on ten-year average produce and prices commuted into cash, came in 1580; 1574 was the Karori experiment.

n183f8e4334a.s: Under Akbar's land classification, land left fallow for one or two years was called:
n183f8e4334a.x: Parauti lay fallow one or two years; Polaj was cultivated every year, Chachar fallow three or four years, Banjar five or more.

ne222862127e.s: Which feature distinguished Mughal mansabdars from the British ICS?
o: They were paid only fixed treasury salaries
ne222862127e.x: Mansabdars held combined civil-military, non-hereditary ranks paid by jagir; the ICS was purely civil and salaried.

n29721e3835c.s: Abul Hasan Tana Shah, the last ruler of Golconda, was exiled to:
n29721e3835c.x: Tana Shah was exiled to Daulatabad and died in 1699; Gwalior was where Murad Bakhsh was imprisoned.

nb2f687c6cf4.s: At Samugarh (1658), Aurangzeb and Murad decisively defeated:
nb2f687c6cf4.x: Samugarh near Agra was the decisive defeat of Dara; Jaswant Singh was beaten at Dharmat and Shuja at Khajwa.

nf9e51334027.s: Dara Shikoh was betrayed to Aurangzeb by:
nf9e51334027.x: Dara was betrayed by Malik Jiwan of Dadar, executed in 1659 and buried in Humayun's Tomb.

nbba482b3e6f.s: Nur Jahan's father, who served as Jahangir's diwan, was:
nbba482b3e6f.x: Ghiyas Beg was Nur Jahan's father and Jahangir's diwan; Asaf Khan was her brother.

nef1e7604a4e.s: Shah Jahan was crowned at Agra in:
nef1e7604a4e.x: Shah Jahan was crowned at Agra in 1628.

nbbe7340d2da.s: Kandahar, recovered by Shah Jahan in 1638, was finally lost to Persia in:
nbbe7340d2da.x: Kandahar was lost under Jahangir, recovered in 1638 and finally lost in 1649.

n44e59c3f239.s: Jahangir lost Kandahar to Persia in:
n44e59c3f239.x: Jahangir annexed neither Kabul nor Kandahar; he lost Kandahar to Persia in 1622.

n3a776db5694.s: The 1636 ahdnamas concluded with Bijapur and Golconda recognised:
n3a776db5694.x: The agreements recognised Mughal suzerainty, required tribute and provided for Mughal arbitration.

n7d56aac593a.x: Nur Jahan married Jahangir in 1611 and received the title Padshah Begum.

ne6fab38c861.s: Jahangir's eldest son Khusrau rebelled in:
ne6fab38c861.x: Khusrau rebelled in 1606; Khurram's revolt (1622-26) was the one provoked by Nur Jahan backing Shahryar.

na9433811f17.x: Jahangir sent Mir Makki; Mir Jumla is linked with Aurangzeb's 1656 attack on Golconda.

nba92238295d.s: The English factory at Surat was established in:
nba92238295d.x: The Surat factory came in 1613, after Captain Best's 1612 victory over the Portuguese off Surat.

n2f28ab9eab5.s: The Nizam Shahi state of Ahmadnagar was annexed by the Mughals in:
n2f28ab9eab5.x: Ahmadnagar was annexed under Shah Jahan in 1636; 1687 is the annexation of Golconda.

n4ff807da693.s: Jahangir gave William Hawkins a mansab and the title:
n4ff807da693.x: Hawkins received the title 'English Khan'; trading rights came later through Sir Thomas Roe.

na49f0e145b7.s: Which Maratha queen is associated with the resistance against Aurangzeb?
na49f0e145b7.x: Shivaji, Sambhaji, Rajaram and Tarabai are all associated with the Maratha resistance against Aurangzeb.

nb106999a9d7.s: After his deposition in 1658, Shah Jahan was kept under guard in:
nb106999a9d7.x: Shah Jahan was confined in Agra Fort and nursed by Jahanara.

nf78680fbff4.s: The Padshahnama of Shah Jahan's reign was written by:
nf78680fbff4.x: Abdul Hamid Lahori wrote the Padshahnama.

nc9fbbd139b6.x: Mumtaz Mahal, born Arjumand Banu Begum, was Asaf Khan's daughter and is entombed in the Taj Mahal.

nindian-history-63-17.s: In Akbar's reign, Salim Chishti is associated with:
nindian-history-63-17.x: Salim Chishti lived at Sikri in Akbar's time.

n2e10647a883.s: The Fatawa-i-Alamgiri was compiled during the reign of:
n2e10647a883.x: The Fatawa-i-Alamgiri belongs to Aurangzeb's reign, not Shah Jahan's 'Golden Age'.

n4a721a22a9b.s: Which of the following contributed to the decline of the Mughal Empire after Aurangzeb?
o: Loss of Bengal to the Marathas
n4a721a22a9b.x: The jagir crisis, along with the Deccan wars and Rajput alienation, contributed to the decline.

ne150b433ccc.s: Sir Thomas Roe's embassy to Jahangir secured for the English:
o: Rights to trade and establish factories
ne150b433ccc.x: Roe obtained rights to trade and set up factories; the title English Khan belonged to William Hawkins.

n312b10b2cd8.s: Which of the following was one of the four subas into which the Mughal Deccan was reorganised?
n312b10b2cd8.x: The four subas were Khandesh, Berar, Telangana and Daulatabad.

n4447377c74e.s: Dara Shikoh was the eldest son of:
n4447377c74e.x: Dara Shikoh was Shah Jahan's eldest son; Jahangir's son was Khusrau.

na8533a97b73.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Mughal conquest of Golconda?
o: Madanna and Akkanna were murdered in 1686.
Its last ruler, Abul Hasan Tana Shah, was exiled to Gwalior.
na8533a97b73.x: Tana Shah was exiled to Daulatabad, not Gwalior (where Murad Bakhsh was imprisoned).

n3ea579f8b33.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Churaman – Jat revolt at Mathura in 1669
Rajaram – Plunder of Akbar's tomb at Sikandra
Satnami revolt – Foundation of Bharatpur power
n3ea579f8b33.x: Rajaram plundered Akbar's tomb; Gokula led the 1669 Mathura revolt, Churaman founded the power that became Bharatpur, and the Satnamis rose at Narnaul.

n7d32bd08c96.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: only one dated item)
n7d32bd08c96.s: Aurangzeb ended music at the imperial court, yet he himself played the:
n7d32bd08c96.x: Aurangzeb banned court music, though Persian works on Indian music were written in his reign and he himself played the veena.

n8ed2193e64b.s: Under Aurangzeb's religious policy, newly built temples were:
n8ed2193e64b.x: Newly built temples were ordered to be destroyed, though court music bans coexisted with Persian works on Indian music.

nf6d30eea9e6.s: Aurangzeb, who died at Ahmednagar in 1707, was buried in a simple grave at:
nf6d30eea9e6.x: He was buried in a simple grave at Khuldabad near Aurangabad, where Tana Shah was also buried.

n5452b29e769.s: The officers Aurangzeb appointed to enforce the Sharia were called:
n5452b29e769.x: Aurangzeb appointed Muhtasibs to enforce the Sharia; he also banned Navroz and discontinued Jharokha darshan.

n01066716c95.s: Jahanara was honoured with the title:
n01066716c95.x: Jahanara was honoured as Sahibat-uz-Zamani (Mistress of the Age); Roshanara was made Padshah Begum.

n0b7f0a9b113.s: Which temple was named in Aurangzeb's temple-demolition order of 1669?
n0b7f0a9b113.x: The 1669 order included Kashi Vishwanath and Keshava Rai at Mathura.

n4c1e3e0a64a.s: The Satnami revolt of 1672 was centred at:
n4c1e3e0a64a.x: The 1672 Satnami revolt of peasants and artisans was centred at Narnaul in Haryana.

nc91faa50ffb.s: Maharaja Jaswant Singh of Marwar, whose death led to the Rajput war of 1679-81, died in:
nc91faa50ffb.x: Jaswant Singh died in 1678; Durgadas Rathore then championed his posthumous heir Ajit Singh.

nd81249528e8.s: Which of the following Mughal central ministers is NOT correctly matched with his work?
o: Wazir or Diwan – Finance and revenue
Mir Bakhshi – Military pay, mansabs and intelligence
Mir Saman – Religion, charity and madad-i-maash grants
Sadr-us-Sudur – Religion, charity and madad-i-maash grants
nd81249528e8.x: The Mir Saman supervised the royal household and karkhanas; religion and charity were under the Sadr-us-Sudur.

neeed2dda9f4.s: Mughal intelligence, run through waqia-navis, khufia-navis and harkaras, came under the:
neeed2dda9f4.x: Intelligence was under the Mir Bakhshi.

nf0fb27d4816.s: A perpetual Mughal jagir grant was called:
nf0fb27d4816.x: Altamgha was perpetual; Tankhwah was in lieu of salary, Watan hereditary in the homeland and Mashrut conditional.

nc544b396e5e.s: Which historian explained the Mughal jagirdari crisis as a shortage of jagirs relative to claimants?
nc544b396e5e.x: Satish Chandra stressed the shortage of jagirs; Irfan Habib the agrarian crisis; Athar Ali the influx of Deccani and Maratha nobles.

o: A grant in lieu of salary
The hereditary home territory of a zamindar or Rajput chief
A grant subject to conditions of service
n2658374aa38.x: Watan jagirs were hereditary home territories and were not transferred by the state.

ncd5e16d4a9d.s: Under Shah Jahan, a jagir yielding half its assessed revenue was termed:
ncd5e16d4a9d.x: A half-yield jagir was shashmaha and a quarter-yield jagir sihmaha.

ne67442f930a.s: By the end of Akbar's reign, the number of subahs had risen to:
ne67442f930a.x: Akbar had 12 subahs in 1580 and 15 by the end of his reign; Aurangzeb had 21.

n7aa0e528da2.s: Under Akbar's Mansabdari system, a mansab denoted:
n7aa0e528da2.x: A mansab was a rank serving military and civil administration, not a hereditary office.

n7f6b0caa1ac.s: Payment to a mansabdar in cash was known as:
n7f6b0caa1ac.x: Mansabdars were paid in cash (naqd) or by non-hereditary assignment of land revenue (jagir).

n2db376343c0.s: The Mughal central administration rested on the mansab, which was a:
n2db376343c0.x: Every officer held a mansab, a combined military-cum-civil rank, which is why the Mughal state was essentially military.

n41d1e177a57.s: In the Mughal Mansabdari system, 'sawar' denoted:
n41d1e177a57.x: Sawar indicated the number of cavalrymen to be maintained; zat was personal rank and status.

n4eea97c12e9.s: In a Mughal province, revenue was managed by the ____, who acted as an independent check on the governor.
n4eea97c12e9.x: The provincial Diwan managed revenue and checked the Subahdar, who handled governance and law and order.

nd1722e42cd4.s: Under the Mansabdari system, ranks and jagirs normally:
o: Ended with the death of the holder
Passed to the holder's eldest son
nd1722e42cd4.x: Mansabs were not hereditary; ranks and jagirs normally ended with the holder's death.

ne6ea4b13c18.s: Gentlemen troopers recruited and paid directly by the Mughal emperor were called:
ne6ea4b13c18.x: Ahadis were recruited directly by the emperor; Tabinan were mansabdars' contingents, dakhili state-paid troops under mansabdars, Walashahi the bodyguard.

nc0856679dd9.s: Jahangir's du-aspa sih-aspa arrangement counted part of a trusted mansabdar's ____ double.
nc0856679dd9.x: Part of the sawar rank was counted twice for trusted mansabdars, without raising their zat.

n6064bc5fc7c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the categories of zamindars in Mughal India?
o: Intermediary zamindars collected revenue from primary zamindars for the state for a commission.
Autonomous chiefs were Rajas ruling their own territories.
Primary zamindars held only temporary, non-hereditary rights over cultivated land.
Autonomous chiefs paid tribute and served as mansabdars.
n6064bc5fc7c.x: Primary zamindars did not hold merely temporary, non-hereditary rights; that statement is false, while the other three are correct.

n34d16037a44.s: Mughal jagirs were revenue assignments given in lieu of:
o: Salary for state, mainly military, service
n34d16037a44.x: Jagirs were revenue assignments in lieu of salary for state service; they were not hereditary and were often transferred.

n397dbcee611.s: A Mughal Sarkar had the Faujdar and the ____ as its principal officials.
n397dbcee611.x: A Sarkar was run by the Faujdar and Amalguzar; a Suba by the Subedar and provincial Diwan.

nfd34aa12002.s: The effective reach of Mughal rural administration generally ended at the:
nfd34aa12002.x: The state's effective reach ended at the Pargana; villages were largely self-governing.

n82b030b5019.s: Under Tana Shah, Qutb Shahi Golconda was divided into how many Sarkars?
n82b030b5019.x: Golconda was organised into tarafs and simalu, with 37 Sarkars and 517 Parganas under Tana Shah.

nb9e5a12fcd8.s: The French traveller and physician who reached Surat in 1666 was:
nb9e5a12fcd8.x: Thevenot reached Surat in 1666; Manucci was Italian, Pelsaert Dutch and Mundy English.

ne34e861abcf.s: In the Mughal period, money-changers and bankers who issued hundis were called:
ne34e861abcf.x: Sarrafs were money-changers and bankers issuing hundis; Mahajans were moneylenders-cum-merchants and Baniks retail traders.

n549015ac2a5.s: Oswals, Maheshwaris and Agarwals belonged to the ____ merchant community.
n549015ac2a5.x: The Marwaris comprised Oswals, Maheshwaris and Agarwals; Chettis were Coromandel merchants.

n90e9394654f.s: Francisco Pelsaert arrived in India in 1620, during the reign of:
n90e9394654f.x: Pelsaert came in Jahangir's time, in 1620.

n4525cf3f6b7.s: Which European traveller held that there was no private property in land in Mughal India?
n4525cf3f6b7.x: Bernier held that private property in land did not exist, a view modern historians have contested.

na047c726521.x: The nobility consisted of high mansabdars, drawn from Turanis, Iranis, Hindustanis and Rajputs.

n4777d5f2eb9.s: Mughal karkhanas, continuing a Sultanate tradition, mainly produced:
n4777d5f2eb9.x: Karkhanas made court luxury goods such as gold and silver articles, fine textiles, arms and jewellery.

ne812bdd35a3.s: One effect of the inflow of silver into Mughal India was:
o: The disappearance of bullion from markets
ne812bdd35a3.x: The silver influx increased silver rupee coinage and raised prices.

n00962cf5210.s: Besides private enterprises, Mughal artisans worked in state workshops called:
n00962cf5210.x: Artisans worked in state karkhanas as well as private enterprises and were often organised in guilds.

n571bf24a3a8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Mughal court customs?
o: Nauroz was a Persian New Year festival adopted from the Zoroastrians.
Jharokha darshan was begun by Akbar and ended by Aurangzeb.
Tuladan weighed the emperor against gold and goods on his birthday.
Sijda and paibos were introduced by Shah Jahan.
n571bf24a3a8.x: Sijda and paibos were introduced by Akbar, not Shah Jahan.

n4477450e8e5.s: Which of the following pairs about Mughal urban society is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Artisans – Worked in state karkhanas and privately
Urban society – Merchants and soldiers only
Physicians, teachers and lawyers – Professional groups
n4477450e8e5.x: Urban society was not made up only of merchants and soldiers; it included artisans and professional groups.

nea9d799122a.s: Mughal nobles, drawn from Turanis, Iranis, Afghans, Hindustanis, Rajputs and Deccanis, remained dependent on:
nea9d799122a.x: The nobles were wealthy but wholly dependent on the emperor's favour.

n19ec77bfad0.s: The tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula at Agra was built by:

n45823559a49.s: In Qutb Shahi Golconda, Muharram was popularly known as:
n45823559a49.x: Muharram was known as Peerla Panduga in Golconda.

nb60d92debd5.s: Who contrasted the strict veiling of Muslim women with the freer movement of Hindu women in A New Account of East India and Persia?
nb60d92debd5.x: John Fryer described this contrast for the Deccan in A New Account of East India and Persia.

n04767c21a61.s: Under Babur and Humayun, the Mughal nobility was dominated by:
n04767c21a61.x: Turanis and Iranis dominated under Babur and Humayun; Akbar added Rajputs and Hindustanis, and Deccanis and Marathas grew under Aurangzeb.

nbf1014be513.s: In the Mughal period, property controlled by Hindu women was known as:
nbf1014be513.x: Hindu women controlled stridhana; Muslim women had inheritance shares and mehr under sharia.

nindian-history-73-15.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts lack dates for all tombs)
nindian-history-73-15.s: Shaikh Salim Chishti's white-marble tomb stands in the Jama Masjid courtyard at:
nindian-history-73-15.x: Salim Chishti's white-marble tomb is in the Jama Masjid courtyard at Fatehpur Sikri.

n9e8049d5bab.s: Agra Fort was begun by Akbar in:
n9e8049d5bab.x: Agra Fort was begun in 1565; Allahabad Fort was built in 1583.

nindian-history-70-13.s: The Gommateshwara statue was built by:

n559b47fdd03.s: The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri (c. 1575) commemorated Akbar's victory in:
n559b47fdd03.x: The Buland Darwaza was built for the Gujarat victory.

nindian-history-26-2-26.s: Pattadakal is a centre of ____ architecture.
nindian-history-26-2-26.x: Pattadakal is Chalukyan; Mahabalipuram is Pallava.

n3e0fcf94311.x: Akbar's Tomb is at Sikandara near Agra.

n99719e6b9d0.s: Fatehpur Sikri served as Akbar's planned capital during:
n99719e6b9d0.x: Fatehpur Sikri was Akbar's capital during 1571-1585 and shows Persian, Indian and Central Asian influences.

nindian-history-26-2-13.s: The temples of Khajuraho belong to ____ architecture.
nindian-history-26-2-13.x: Khajuraho is Chandela; Thanjavur is Chola and Mahabalipuram Pallava.

nindian-history-86-14.s: The Panch Mahal at Fatehpur Sikri was built by:
nindian-history-86-14.x: The Panch Mahal, Buland Darwaza and Jama Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri are Akbar's.

nindian-history-10-5.s: The Bahmani Kingdom shifted its capital from Gulbarga to:
nindian-history-10-5.x: The Bahmanis moved their capital from Gulbarga to Bidar.

nindian-history-10-16.x: Shivaji's capital was Raigad; Pune was the centre of Peshwa power.

nindian-history-73-18.s: Rabia-ud-Daurani, whose tomb is the Bibi ka Maqbara, was Aurangzeb's:
nindian-history-73-18.x: Rabia-ud-Daurani was Aurangzeb's wife; their son Azam Shah built the tomb for his mother.

nindian-history-86-12.s: The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque was built by:
nindian-history-86-12.x: The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque was built by Sher Shah Suri; Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal, Red Fort and Jama Masjid, Delhi.

nindian-history-73-12.s: Nur Jahan built the marble tomb of her father Itmad-ud-Daula at Agra during:
nindian-history-73-12.x: The tomb of Itmad-ud-Daula (Mirza Ghiyas Beg) was built in 1622-1628.

n497a9f9093f.s: The Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga is noted for its:
n497a9f9093f.x: Its fully covered courtyard sets it apart from the open-court pattern of Mughal mosques.

naf7afbd1dfd.s: The Red Fort Complex was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in:
naf7afbd1dfd.x: Red Fort Complex: 2007; Agra Fort and Taj Mahal: 1983; Fatehpur Sikri: 1986; Humayun's Tomb: 1993.

n5b15f7a546c.s: Pietra dura was first used on a large scale in Mughal architecture at:
n5b15f7a546c.x: Pietra dura began under Jahangir, appeared on a large scale at Itimad-ud-Daula and peaked at the Taj Mahal.

n972a6a2eeec.s: The Peacock Throne in the Diwan-i-Khas of the Red Fort was taken by Nadir Shah in:
n972a6a2eeec.x: Nadir Shah took the Peacock Throne from the Diwan-i-Khas, the private audience hall, in 1739.

n98f60cbc17b.s: Which of the following is a Qutb Shahi monument rather than a Mughal one?
n98f60cbc17b.x: Golconda Fort is Qutb Shahi; the other three are listed UNESCO Mughal sites.

n6308539dfa9.s: The Moti Masjid in Agra Fort was built by:
n6308539dfa9.x: The Agra Fort Moti Masjid is Shah Jahan's; Aurangzeb built the one in the Red Fort, Delhi.

na3d174bcf61.s: The Char Minar is located at:
na3d174bcf61.x: The Char Minar is in Hyderabad.

nc2c6332e1cc.x: Jahangir's tomb is at Shahdara, Lahore; Akbar's is at Sikandra and Aurangzeb's at Khuldabad.

nindian-history-71-2.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts carry no dates)
nindian-history-71-2.s: The Tabriz-born master who first led work on the Hamzanama was:
nindian-history-71-2.x: Mir Sayyid Ali of Tabriz first led the Hamzanama; Abdus Samad (Shirin Qalam) later headed the atelier.

n63d264b8786.s:
Arrange these emphases of Mughal painting in chronological order:
1. Portraits, albums, flora, fauna and naturalism
2. Foundation through Persian masters
3. Formal court scenes, albums and floral borders
4. Illustrated manuscripts and a large painting atelier
n63d264b8786.x: Humayun (Persian masters), Akbar (illustrated manuscripts), Jahangir (naturalism), Shah Jahan (formal court scenes): 2-4-1-3.

nindian-history-71-12.s: The Kangra sub-school of Pahari painting peaked under:
nindian-history-71-12.x: Kangra flourished under Raja Sansar Chand.

n1bb6d004c7a.s: In the Sultanate period, the language of administration, diplomacy and high culture was:
n1bb6d004c7a.x: Persian replaced Sanskrit and Arabic in official and elite functions, while Hindavi grew in camps and bazaars.

nindian-history-85-17.s: The Tarikh-i-Alfi is a history of:
o: The first thousand years of Islam
nindian-history-85-17.x: Tarikh-i-Alfi covers Islam's first millennium; the Akbarnama is Abul Fazl's history of Akbar.

nd81e19eff18.s: The Sur Sagar was written by:
nd81e19eff18.x: Surdas wrote Sur Sagar; Tulsidas wrote Ramcharitmanas and Rahim composed Hindi dohas.

nindian-history-71-8.s: The Mughal painter titled Nadir-ul-Asra was:
nindian-history-71-8.x: Ustad Mansur was Nadir-ul-Asra; Abul Hasan was Nadir-ul-Zaman.

n4fab9981913.x: Mirza Muhammad Kazim wrote the Alamgirnama; Lahori wrote the Padshahnama.

n407e8338269.s: The Sayyid brothers, Abdullah Khan and Husain Ali Khan, were overthrown with the help of:
n407e8338269.x: They were overthrown with the help of Nizam-ul-Mulk, not Murshid Quli Khan.

n3a63229651a.s: The painter Basawan belonged to the atelier of:
n3a63229651a.x: Basawan belonged to Akbar's reign; Jahangir's painters included Manohar, Bishandas and Mansur.

nindian-history-13-26.x: Abul Fazl wrote Ayar-i-Danish; Kashifi wrote Anwar-i-Suhaili and Nasrullah Shirazi Kalila-wa-Dimnah.

n787db370aa4.s: The first Urdu poetic diwan is associated with:
n787db370aa4.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah is known for the first Urdu poetic diwan; Dakhni grew as a literary medium under the Qutb Shahis.

n7b9168d3c34.s: The Pahari school of painting (17th-19th centuries) was associated with:
n7b9168d3c34.x: Pahari painting flourished in the Sub-Himalayan region; the Bahmani link belongs to Deccani painting.

naafdbb1e19e.s: When Aurangzeb withdrew patronage, painters moved to Rajasthan, the Punjab Hills and:
naafdbb1e19e.x: Painters moved to Rajasthan, the Punjab Hills and Bihar; Bengal is not part of this association.

n062760e4ca9.s: Akbar's painting atelier of more than 100 painters was known as the:
n062760e4ca9.x: The Tasvir Khana illustrated the Hamzanama, Tutinama, Akbarnama and Razmnama.

n8360e85f558.s: Which Persian master did Humayun bring to India to lay the foundation of the Mughal school of painting?
n8360e85f558.x: Humayun brought Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad; Basawan was Akbar-era and Mansur of Jahangir's court.

nd39b62cf236.x: Khafi Khan wrote the Muntakhab-ul-Lubab; Badauni wrote the Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh.

n73c00d23f61.s: Which Mughal emperor ended court music yet himself played the veena?
n73c00d23f61.x: Aurangzeb ended court music, but Persian works on classical music were produced in his reign and he played the veena.

n8f9f340f65d.s: Manohar, a portrait painter of the Akbar-Jahangir period, was the son of:
n8f9f340f65d.x: Manohar was the son of Basawan, a leading master of Akbar's court.

nindian-history-85-19.s: The Molla Ramayanam is a work in:
nindian-history-85-19.x: Molla Ramayanam is a Telugu work, unlike the Persian Razmnama and Persian Ramayana of Akbar's time.

nindian-history-85-18.s: Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas is a devotional poem in:
nindian-history-85-18.x: Ramcharitmanas is an Awadhi devotional poem, not a Mughal court manuscript.

n441efa8c620.s: Tansen, one of Akbar's Navaratnas, was honoured with the title:
n441efa8c620.x: Tansen moved from Raja Ramchandra of Rewa's court to Akbar's and was honoured as 'Mian'.

n41299f0b9d9.s: Under Akbar, the Atharvaveda was translated into Persian by:
n41299f0b9d9.x: Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi translated the Atharvaveda; Badauni and Naqib Khan worked on the Razmnama.

nindian-history-23-2-16.s: Akbar's Translation Department, which rendered Sanskrit, Arabic, Turkish and Greek works into Persian, was supervised by:

nindian-history-71-6.s: The Dastan-i-Amir Hamza, begun under Humayun, comprised about how many paintings?
nindian-history-71-6.x: The Hamzanama took about 100 artists and about 1,400 paintings, supervised by Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad.

nindian-history-13-25.s: Babur's autobiography, the Tuzuk-i-Baburi, is also known as the:
nindian-history-13-25.x: Tuzuk-i-Baburi, also called the Baburnama, is Babur's autobiography in Chagatai Turkish.

nindian-history-71-15.s: Which school of painting, a later indigenous Bengal style, was NOT shaped by Mughal painting?
nindian-history-71-15.x: Mughal painting influenced the Pahari, Rajasthani and Kangra schools; Kalighat was a later indigenous Bengal style.

n6bbc94b2f4d.s: Under the Qutb Shahis, the growth of Kuchipudi is associated with:
n6bbc94b2f4d.x: Kuchipudi's growth is associated with Siddhendra Yogi; Persian was the official language and Telugu the people's language.

n1366a977e5a.s: Muted naturalistic colours, perspective and shading are characteristic of ____ painting.
n1366a977e5a.x: Mughal painting used muted naturalistic colours, perspective and shading; Rajput painting was vivid and decorative.

n76a4048e33b.s: The third volume of Abul Fazl's Akbarnama is known as the:
n76a4048e33b.x: The Akbarnama has three volumes, the third being the Ain-i-Akbari.

n061d1bc6b2d.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Chin Qilich Khan – Nizam of Hyderabad
n061d1bc6b2d.x: Safdar Jung was associated with Awadh, not Hyderabad; Chin Qilich Khan was the Nizam of Hyderabad.

n7d379d8a893.s:
Assertion (A): The foundations of the Mughal Empire were weakened after Aurangzeb.
Reason (R): Aurangzeb's long Deccan wars drained the treasury.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n7d379d8a893.x: The prolonged Deccan wars drained the treasury and weakened the empire's foundations, so R explains A.

nindian-history-11-13.s: Babur took the title 'Padshah' at Kabul in:
nindian-history-11-13.x: Babur became Padshah at Kabul in 1507 and took the title Ghazi after Khanwa in 1527.

nedf244e899c.s: Ghulam Qadir Rohilla blinded which Mughal emperor in 1788?
nedf244e899c.x: Shah Alam II was blinded by Ghulam Qadir; Ahmad Shah was blinded by Imad-ul-Mulk and Farrukh Siyar by the Sayyids.

n5c490c3b292.s: Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan, founder of the Asaf Jahi state, defeated Mubariz Khan at:
n5c490c3b292.x: He defeated Mubariz Khan at Shakar Kheda; the state was founded in 1724.

nindian-history-21-4.s: Muhammad Ghori first invaded India in:
nindian-history-21-4.x: Muhammad Ghori's first invasion was in 1175.

n772f362a05b.s: Under the Treaty of Allahabad, Shah Alam II was entitled to an annual payment of:
n772f362a05b.x: Shah Alam II received Kora and Allahabad and Rs 26 lakh a year, which Warren Hastings stopped from 1772.

n303b94677ce.s: Nadir Shah invaded India during the reign of:
n303b94677ce.x: Nadir Shah invaded in 1739, during Muhammad Shah's reign.

nindian-history-141-11.s: Who fought the battles of Tarain and Chandawar?
nindian-history-141-11.x: Muhammad Ghori fought at Tarain and Chandawar; Mahmud Ghazni made 17 raids.

nindian-history-67-6.s: The Persian invasion of north-western India was led by:
nindian-history-67-6.x: Darius I led the Persian invasion; Alexander led the Greek one.

nf485fd19504.s: Safdar Jung, who succeeded Saadat Khan as Nawab of Awadh, was Saadat Khan's:
nf485fd19504.x: Safdar Jung was Saadat Khan's nephew and son-in-law and also became Wazir.

nindian-history-141-22.s: The Huna ruler Mihirakula was defeated by:

n07d38ca7a39.s: The Carnatic state of Arcot was founded by:
n07d38ca7a39.x: Arcot was founded by Saadatullah Khan; Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk founded Awadh.

nb425a4dcf74.s: Shah Alam II returned to Delhi in 1771-72 under the protection of:
nb425a4dcf74.x: After living at Allahabad under Company protection, Shah Alam II returned to Delhi under Mahadji Scindia's protection.

nindian-history-67-15.s: Alexander defeated Porus at the battle of the:
nindian-history-67-15.x: Alexander defeated Porus at the Hydaspes.

nindian-history-67-13.s: Nadir Shah defeated the Mughals at the Battle of Karnal in:
nindian-history-67-13.x: In 1739 Nadir Shah won at Karnal and then sacked Delhi.

nindian-history-21-21.s: Along with Shah Jahan's Peacock Throne, Nadir Shah carried away the:
nindian-history-21-21.x: In 1739 Nadir Shah sacked Delhi and carried away the Koh-i-Noor and the Peacock Throne.

nindian-history-21-18.s: The Third Battle of Panipat was fought in:
nindian-history-21-18.x: Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani) defeated the Marathas at Third Panipat in 1761.

nindian-history-21-5.s: The First Battle of Tarain was fought in:
nindian-history-21-5.x: First Tarain was fought in 1191; Timur came in 1398, Panipat I was 1526 and Karnal 1739.

n14e7e35a354.s: After helping overthrow the Sayyid brothers, Nizam-ul-Mulk appointed ____ as Diwan.
n14e7e35a354.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk helped overthrow the Sayyids and appointed Puran Chand as Diwan.

nd38503e56ae.s: Ahmad Shah Abdali's raids into India began from:
nd38503e56ae.x: Abdali's raids began in 1748 and culminated at Panipat in 1761; Nadir Shah raided in 1739.

ne02fac11147.s: Punjab and Multan were ceded to Ahmad Shah Abdali, who invaded repeatedly during the reign of:
ne02fac11147.x: Abdali's repeated invasions occurred during Alamgir II's reign.

n67fa00cff3a.s: Among the Sayyid brothers, Husain Ali Khan held the post of:
n67fa00cff3a.x: Husain Ali Khan was Mir Bakhshi and Abdullah Khan the Wazir; they dominated Mughal politics from 1713 to 1720.

nfd2ee8728b4.s: The first Mughal pensioner of the East India Company was:
nfd2ee8728b4.x: Shah Alam II became the Company's first Mughal pensioner.

n6624d222e1d.s: Hyderabad State was integrated into the Indian Union in 1948 through:
n6624d222e1d.x: Operation Polo integrated Hyderabad in 1948; Mir Osman Ali Khan was the last Nizam.

nb94d0d3952e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the rise of the Marathas?
o: The Sahyadri hills and hill forts favoured guerrilla warfare.
Bhakti saints promoted spiritual and regional unity.
Aurangzeb's Deccan campaign strengthened Mughal finances.
Marathas had served in the armies and revenue offices of the Deccan Sultanates.
nb94d0d3952e.x: Aurangzeb's 27-year Deccan campaign drained the Mughal treasury rather than strengthening it.

n758dd965a55.s: Which of the following Ashtapradhan titles is wrongly matched with its portfolio?
o: Waqia-navis – Intelligence and the king's diary
n758dd965a55.x: The Dabir (Sumant) handled foreign affairs; treasury and revenue belonged to the Amatya.

nd09f0bfe492.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts carry one date)
nd09f0bfe492.s: The Mughal grants of 1719 gave the Marathas chauth and sardeshmukhi of how many Deccan subas?
nd09f0bfe492.x: The 1719 grants recognised Shahu, confirmed Swarajya lands and gave chauth and sardeshmukhi of the six Deccan subas.

n7d5118dc677.s: Samarth Ramdas, traditionally named as Shivaji's guru, wrote the:
n7d5118dc677.x: Samarth Ramdas wrote the Dasbodh; Shivaji's guardian was Dadaji Kondadev.

n6a6405e70d3.s: Shivaji's coronation at Raigad took place in:
n6a6405e70d3.x: Coronation 1674; second Surat raid 1670; treaty with Tana Shah 1677; death 1680.

n155ac8a1d3e.s: The Nizam conceded Maratha claims to chauth and sardeshmukhi at:
n155ac8a1d3e.x: The Nizam conceded chauth and sardeshmukhi at Palkhed; the Mughals had conceded them in 1719.

n95f0d26df1d.s: Rajaram, who created the post of Pratinidhi, directed Maratha resistance against Aurangzeb from:
n95f0d26df1d.x: Rajaram directed resistance from Gingee (Jinji) and drew Aurangzeb south.

n4dab091078f.s: In Shivaji's Ashtapradhan, the Nyayadhish was the:
o: Keeper of intelligence and the king's diary
n4dab091078f.x: The Nyayadhish was the chief justice; the Amatya handled finance, the Panditrao religion and the Mantri intelligence.

n319e7f3f45d.s: Tarabai's line was later settled at Kolhapur under the Treaty of:
n319e7f3f45d.x: Tarabai's line was settled at Kolhapur under the Treaty of Warna.

naa2a638dc6f.s: Shivaji's sea forts such as Sindhudurg, Kolaba and Vijaydurg guarded the ____ coast.
naa2a638dc6f.x: The sea forts guarded the Konkan coast; Shivaji is called the Father of the Indian Navy.

nd112f754963.x: Bagayat was irrigated land, Jirayat dry land and Kathi a measuring rod.

nf2d069e0c8f.s: Maratha cavalrymen who were given horses and equipment by the state were called:
nf2d069e0c8f.x: Bargirs were state-equipped cavalry; Shiledars maintained their own horses.

n937fb6add13.s: In Golconda, Akkanna held the post of:
n937fb6add13.x: Akkanna was Sar Lashkar and Madanna the Mir Jumla of Golconda.

nfe1acff2ca4.s: Shivaji's Ashtapradhan was ____, whereas the Mughal wazir system was hierarchical.
nfe1acff2ca4.x: The Ashtapradhan was advisory and the Mughal wazir system hierarchical; Shivaji also paid in cash rather than jagirs.

n4f45e3fc141.s: During his escape from house arrest at Agra in 1666, Shivaji was accompanied by:
n4f45e3fc141.x: Shivaji escaped together with Sambhaji, hidden in baskets of sweets and fruit.

n7684e7e93db.s: Balaji Vishwanath was appointed Peshwa in 1713 by:
n7684e7e93db.x: Shahu appointed Balaji Vishwanath (Peshwa 1713-20); real power then shifted from the Chhatrapati to the Peshwa.

n986ef709eb1.s: The service land grants that Shivaji abolished but which returned under Shahu and the Peshwas were called:
n986ef709eb1.x: Shivaji abolished jagirs and paid in cash; saranjam grants returned under Shahu and the Peshwas.

nade54945415.s: At his coronation, Shivaji adopted the title:
nade54945415.x: The coronation title was 'Shri Raja Shiva Chhatrapati'; he was also styled Haindava Dharmoddharak, not Hindavi Sultan.

n257ebf1b2f7.s: Under Shivaji, Marathi administrative records were kept in the ____ script.
n257ebf1b2f7.x: Marathi and Sanskrit were promoted over Persian, and the cursive Modi script was used for Marathi records.

nfdd4c42e546.s: At the Battle of Salher in 1672, the Marathas defeated in open battle the:
nfdd4c42e546.x: At Salher in 1672 the Marathas defeated the Mughals in open battle.

n4d0964fb872.s: At its peak, the Maratha Empire extended from Attock to:
n4d0964fb872.x: The Maratha Empire ran from Attock to Cuttack and from the Gulf of Khambhat to beyond the Kaveri.

n1038d4f73a1.s: The burden of paying chauth after the 1795 war pushed the Nizam into the British Subsidiary Alliance in:
n1038d4f73a1.x: After the 1795 war the Nizam paid chauth to the Marathas, which contributed to his joining the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.

n4a550b094e3.s: Shivaji's revenue settlement, in which the state dealt directly with the cultivator, was of the ____ type.
n4a550b094e3.x: Shivaji dealt directly with cultivators in a ryotwari-type settlement and paid officials in cash.

n5173a666be7.s: In 1659 Shivaji killed the Bijapur general Afzal Khan at the foot of:
n5173a666be7.x: Shivaji killed Afzal Khan with a wagh nakh at the foot of Pratapgad.

n6d6775736e2.s: In his southern campaign, Shivaji took Gingee, Ballari and:
n6d6775736e2.x: Shivaji took Gingee, Vellore and Ballari and refused to share the spoils.

nc81043a3f9c.s: The Treaty of Purandar (1665) was concluded by Shivaji with:
nc81043a3f9c.x: Shivaji signed the Treaty of Purandar with Raja Jai Singh (Mirza Raja of Amber), surrendering 23 of his 35 forts.

nb0fd03b0e6d.s: In Shivaji's Ashtapradhan, every minister reported directly to the:
nb0fd03b0e6d.x: Each minister reported to the Chhatrapati; posts were not hereditary and ministers could be transferred or dismissed.
